description: Three-quarter-length silk dress. The centre front panel of the bodice is black with three large pale blue buttons. The edges of the bodice, peplum, and cuffs are trimmed with a silver braid outline. Frank Sharman Photographic Collection
creator: Frank Sharman

metadata.Date notes: Material undated; dates derived through research.
metadata.Extent: 16 files of black and white prints (100 items); 14 files of colour transparencies (199 items); 22 files of black and white negatives (394 strips)
metadata.Scope and content: The collection contains colour transparencies and black and white prints and negatives of performances by English and foreign ballet companies performing in London: Sadler's Wells Ballet, Sadler's Wells Opera Ballet, Ballet Rambert, Les Ballets des Champs-Elysées, Les Ballets de Paris, International Ballet, Marquis de Cuevas' Grand Ballet de Monte Carlo, and Original Ballet Russe. There are also three images of the Covent Garden Opera Company. Sharman took many of the photographs from the theatres' balconies, although most of the colour photographs were taken during dress rehearsals from the stalls. The collection is notable for the colour photographs, shot with Kodrachrome film, which have retained their brilliant colour.
metadata.Creator: Frank Sharman
metadata.History/biography: English photographer Frank Sharman, F.R.P.S. (1904-84) took photographs of ballet companies performing in London between 1946 and 1950. Rare in a black-and-white era, Sharman used Kodachrome film to record ballet productions in colour, which has meant that the vibrancy and accuracy of the colour has lasted. Sharman also took black and white 'action' photographs of dancers during performance, usually shooting from the balcony. It is not known whether Sharman was a professional photographer in the 1940s, or trying to establish a career in ballet photography. His ballet photographs were published irregularly in 'The Dancing Times', 'Ballet Today', and 'Dance Magazine', and more frequently in 'Ballet Annual'. His images also appeared in International Ballet's souvenir programme for May 1950 and in the booklet 'The Story of Swan Lake' (E.G. Derrington, St. Clements Press, London, 1948), which featured International Ballet's production. Sharman joined the Royal Photographic Society in 1941 and it is believed he became a Fellow of the society with a panel of ballet photographs. He remained a member until his death in 1984. At the end of his working life, Sharman was the British agent for a German paper mill and a keen amateur photographer. He was President of the Beckenham Photographic Society, 1953-1955, and a member until 1971. Sharman was a regular speaker on the society's annual programme of meetings, and in 1961, he gave a talk entitled 'Twenty-one years of Colour'.
metadata.Source of acquisition: The collection was donated in memory of Ethel Sharman, wife of Frank Sharman, by her estate.
metadata.System of arrangement: The collection is divided by material type into three categories: black and white photographic prints, colour transparencies, and black and white photographic negatives. Within each series, the images are grouped by company and then alphabetically by production. All prints and transparencies have been scanned and attached to item-level catalogue records. A selection of images from the negatives have been scanned and attached to file-level catalogue records.
metadata.Access conditions: The collection, which includes large copy prints of 'The Sleeping Beauty' transparencies, is available for viewing in ROH Collections by appointment only.
metadata.Copyright: Copyright is owned by Royal Opera House Collections.

title: Lady de Grey Photographic Collection
creator: Constance Gwladys (Lady de Grey) | Marchioness of Ripon Robinson
condition: Good. Most items are exhibiting foxing; a few photographs are faded.

metadata.Date notes: It would appear that Lady de Grey collected the photographs and postcards between the early 1880s and 1913. The earliest dated photograph is 1883, although research suggests that some items could be a few years earlier. The latest dated photograph is 1913. It is likely that Lady de Grey put the photographs and postcards into the two albums during World War I, when the Royal Opera House was closed and travel to Europe was difficult. Evidence for this is that the albums do not run chronologically, that her captions are in the same handwriting and pen, and in the past tense. Lady de Grey died in 1917.
metadata.Extent: 8 boxes containing 116 sepia photographic prints, 36 black and white photographic prints, 2 colour-tinted photographic prints, 15 sepia postcards, 6 black and white postcards, 1 paper postcard, 1 sketch, 1 magazine cutting, and 2 newspaper cuttings
metadata.Scope and content: Portraits of people in the arts, many signed and inscribed by the subject. The majority are studio portraits. There are two amateur 'snapshots' and two other outdoor photographs. Lady de Grey wrote captions under most of the images. The people depicted are: Singers: Emma Albani, Albert Alvarez, Max Alvary, Mario Ancona, Giuseppe Anselmi, Alessandro Bonci, Hans Breuer, Alois Burgstaller, Emma Calvé, Enrico Caruso, Lina Cavalieri, Féodor Chaliapine, Emmy Destinn, Ernest Van Dyck, Emma Eames, Fritz Friedrichs, Julián Gayarre, Jeanne Granier, Jacques Isnardon, Roxo Betty Kalisch, Jean Lassalle, Julius Lieban, Fernando de Lucia, Victor Maurel, Nellie Melba, Alice Nielsen, Lillian Nordica, Marguerite Zinah de Nuovina, Adelina Patti, Pol Plançon, Margaret Reed, Marie Renard, Edouard de Reszke, Jean de Reszke, Renée Richard, Anton van Rooy, Titta Ruffo, Albert Saleza, Sibyl Sanderson, Karl Scheidemantel, Antonio Scotti, Rosa Sucher, Francesco Tamagno, Heinrich Vogl, and Marie Van Zandt. Composers: Herman Bemberg, Arrigo Boito, Cécile Chaminade, Mario Pasquale Costa, Gabriel Fauré, Charles-François Gounod, Reynaldo Hahn, Ruggero Leoncavallo, Pietro Mascagni, Giacomo Puccini, Paul Alfred Rubens, Arthur Goring Thomas, Ambroise Thomas, and Francesco Paolo Tosti. Conductors: Tymoteusz Adamowski, Ernesto Bevignani, Cleofonte Campanini, Luigi Mancinelli, Alberto Randegger, Hans Richter, and Anton Seidl. Actors: Marie Effie Bancroft, Jeanne Bartet, Marthe Brandés, Lucien Guitry, Jane Hading, Cora Brown Potter, Gabrielle Réjane, and Ellen Terry. Writers: Alexandre Dumas (fils), Victor Hugo, Edward Bulmer-Lytton, Arthur Wing Pinero, Ernest Renan, and Jean Porto-Rico. Others: dancer Vaslav Nijinsky, artists Jean Béraud and Franz von Lenbach, impresarios Maurice Grau and Augustus Harris, musicians Mischa Elman and Joseph Hollman, opera director Pierre Gailhard, French statesman Léon Gambetta, mime artist Felicia Mallet, music publisher Tito Ricordi, members of the de Reszke family, and Lady de Grey herself.
metadata.Creator: Constance Gwladys (Lady de Grey) | Marchioness of Ripon Robinson
metadata.History/biography: Constance Gwladys Robinson, Marchioness of Ripon, was born the Honorable Constance Gwladys Herbert on 24 April 1859. She was the youngest daughter of Sidney Herbert, 1st Baron Herbert of Lea, and Mary Elizabeth A'Court-Repington. In 1878, Constance Gwladys Herbert married St George Henry Lowther, 4th Earl of Lonsdale (1855-1882), by whom she had one daughter, Lady Gladys Mary Juliet Lowther (1881-1965), known as Juliet. In 1885, Lady Lonsdale married Frederick Oliver Robinson, 4th Earl de Grey (1852-1923) and became Lady de Grey. When her husband became the 2nd Marquis of Ripon in 1909, she became Marchioness of Ripon (sometimes known as Lady Ripon). Lady de Grey was a leading London hostess and member of the Prince of Wales’s circle. Through her influence, Augustus Harris was made manager of the Royal Italian Opera in 1888, and the theatre’s fortunes began to improve after a period of decline. Lady de Grey’s patronage gave her influence over all major decisions, including the commissioning of new operas, the engagement of singers, and the granting of box subscriptions. She supported Harris in his decision to introduce performances of opera in its native tongue (when previously all opera was performed in Italian translation); this led to the company being re-named the Royal Opera House in 1892. Lady de Grey was friendly with many of the famous singers of the day. She was particularly close friends with Nellie Melba, whom she introduced to Covent Garden after seeing her perform at the Théâtre de la Monnaie. Following an unsuccessful début performance in 1888, Melba was initially reluctant to return, but with Lady de Grey’s persuasion she was encouraged to sing again a year later to great acclaim. In 1901 Lord de Grey acquired Coombe Court at Kingston, one of his many residences. This venue became well-known for the dinner parties hosted by Lady de Grey, to which singers from the Royal Opera House and notable figures were invited. Invitations were sent long in advance to ensure she obtained her ideal choice of guests. After seeing Diaghilev’s Ballet Russes in its debut in Paris in 1907, Lady de Grey was determined to bring the company to London, resulting in the historic season of Russian ballet at Covent Garden in 1911. It is said that Lady de Grey was present every time Nijinsky danced. When the activities of the Royal Opera House were halted during World War I, Lady de Grey devoted her time instead to the King George Hospital, where she worked daily caring for injured servicemen. Shortly before her death on 27 October 1917, she was working to establish a scheme for the care of paralysed and disabled soldiers near their own homes.
metadata.Archival history: The two albums were in the possession of Lady de Grey's daughter, Juliet Trevor (by her second marriage - Lady Juliet Duff by her first). Upon Juliet's death in 1965, the albums passed to her son, Sir Michael Duff. That same year, he gave them to Desmond Shawe-Taylor, the music critic and author, who had been a close friend of his mother. Shawe-Taylor initially bequeathed the albums to the Royal Opera House, but in 1992 he deposited the collection after conservation work. The conservation, undertaken by Kate Colleran and Marcel Ciantar in 1990 and 1991, involved removing the items and Lady de Grey's captions from the albums and re-creating the pages on archival boards with mounts. The conservators took photographs of the original pages, which were deposited with the collection.
metadata.System of arrangement: Lady de Grey compiled her photographs and postcards in two large leather-bound albums. During conservation, the images and her captions were removed and mounted on archival board, following their layout in the albums. Each page became a separate mount. The mounts are stored in eight boxes in the order in which the pages appeared in the albums.

She wore this dress in both productions.]

title: Dress worn by Margot Fonteyn as Raymonda in The Royal Ballet production of 'Raymonda Scène d'amour' (1960)

The boned bodice is ruched and trimmed at the neckline with a band of gilt braid leaves set with faux pearls and faux amber stones. It has a central medallion of rhinestones and faux aquamarines. The waistband is made of dark brown net and two bands of gold braid and lace decorated with faux pearls and gems. The long chiffon sleeves are slashed and embroidered with gold braid in the form of fronds. The skirt is decorated with large opalescent sequins. There are elastic shoulder straps. Worn with headdress ROH/PRO/COS/0003462. [Note: Fonteyn first danced this role at a gala for the Royal Academy of Dancing in November 1959 and subsequently with The Royal Ballet in March 1960. She wore this dress in both productions.]

Kennedy in Houston, Texas, October/November 1964; previews and articles relating to the new ballet 'Home' featuring Nadia Nerina with the Western Theatre Ballet at the Sunderland Empire, December 1964; copy of a programme for 'Home', December 1964; cuttings relating to the fire at Nadia Nerina's London home, December 1964; reviews of the redesigned Royal Ballet Touring Company production of 'Swan Lake' with Nadia Nerina and Attilio Labis, May 1965; reviews of The Royal Ballet performances of 'Swan Lake' at the New Theatre, Oxford, October 1965; cuttings of Nadia Nerina in fashionable attire at the airport on her way to Milan for British Week, October 1965; reviews of The Royal Ballet in 'Swan Lake' at Manchester Opera House, November 1965; cuttings relating to Nadia Nerina being involved in a car crash near Banbury, Oxfordshire, January 1966; cuttings relating to Nadia Nerina appearing on the Ed Sullivan Show in the USA, April 1966; announcements that Nadia Nerina is to retire as a resident ballerina and become a Guest Artist of The Royal Ballet, August 1966; previews of the Royal Variety Show cast, October 1966; reviews of the Royal Variety Performance at the London Palladium with Nadia Nerina and Christopher Gable and Royal Ballet dancers performing an excerpt from 'La Fille mal gardée', November 1966; cuttings relating to Nadia Nerina leaving London to dance in 'Swan Lake' with the American Ballet Theatre, Chicago, February 1967; programme of the American Ballet Theatre production of 'Swan Lake'; USA press reviews of 'Swan Lake', February 1967; previews to promote Nadia Nerina's appearance in a Gala performance of 'Giselle' at the Stadt-theater, Basel, April 1967; reviews of Nadia Nerina in 'Dragonfly' and 'The Dying Swan' with Harlequin Ballet Company, April 1967.

title: Magazine cuttings and ephemera collected by Nadia Nerina
dimensions: length 39 cm; width 25.5 cm; depth 11 cm

metadata.Date notes: Undated.
metadata.Scope and content: Black and white cuttings from magazines including pictures of the Sadler's Wells Ballet production of 'The Sleeping Beauty' featuring Beryl Grey, Michael Somes, Moira Shearer, and Jack Hart; cuttings from magazines of Sadler's Wells Ballet and The Royal Ballet productions of 'Swan Lake', 'Symphonic Variations', 'Scènes de ballet' 'Apparitions', 'Checkmate', 'Les Sirènes', 'Dante Sonata', 'Hamlet', 'Adam Zero', 'Miracle in the Gorbals', 'The Rake's Progress', 'Coppélia', 'Les Sylphides', 'Three-Cornered Hat' and 'Ballet Imperial'; cuttings of pictures of Anna Pavlova, Margot Fonteyn, Alicia Markova, Anton Dolin, and various dancers of the Sadler's Wells Ballet and Sadler's Wells Theatre Ballet including Pamela May, Brian Shaw, Donald Britten, Alexander Grant, Robert Helpmann, June Brae, Harold Turner, Julia Farron, Leslie Edwards, and Frederick Ashton; small poster of the Sadler's Wells Ballet performance at the Metropolitan Opera House, New York, 9 October-6 November 1949; Dance News feature on the first Sadler's Wells Ballet tour to the USA, October 1949; menu from the Dining Car Service enroute to Houston Texas on the Sadler's Wells Ballet tour of America, 1949; cuttings of pictures of the American Ballet Theatre productions of 'Jones Beach', 'Bourée fantasque', 'Les Présages', 'Rouge et noir', 'Pillar of Fire', 'Billy the Kid' and 'Graduation Ball' featuring Maria Tallchief, Rosella Hightower, George Skibine, Nora Kaye, Hugh Laing, and Michael Kidd; cuttings of pictures of Les Ballets des Champs-Elysées productions of 'Le Jeunne homme et la mort' and 'Les Forains'; cuttings of pictures of dancers including Marina Semyonova, Yvette Chauviré, Léonide Massine, Alicia Alonso, Vaslav Nijinsky, Marie Rambert, Constantin Tcherkas, Freddie Franklin, Alexandra Danilova, Patricia Miller, Pirmin Trecu, David Poole, Philip Chatfield, Elaine Fifield, Sheilah O'Reilly, John Cranko, Rowena Jackson, Tamara Toumanova, Mikhail Fokine; cuttings of pictures of various Russian dancers; a signed picture of Maris Liepa; greetings card from Ninette de Valois to Nadia Nerina, 6th May 1956; Christmas card from Cyril Beaumont to Nadia Nerina featuring a photograph of Marie Taglioni; colour postcards of San Fransisco, the Columbia River Oregon and South Africa; Wedding anniversary cards; Christmas cards; other greetings cards; 21st birthday card from Anne [Negus] and Beryl [Grey]; museum postcards of artwork; watercolour scenes and possible set designs by an unknown artist; cuttings of pictures of general interest from magazines.

title: Programmes from Galas featuring Nadia Nerina at the Royal Opera House, Covent Garden
Programme of a Covent Garden Opera Trust State Peformance at the Royal Opera House Covent Garden to mark the visit of Vincent Auriol the President of The French Republic, 9 March 1950

metadata.Date notes: Programme is dated.
metadata.Scope and content: Gala programme listing the evening's programme of performances as 'Symphonic Variations', 'Façade', and 'The Sleeping Beauty Act III' and concluding with La Marseillaise and God Save the King. Nadia Nerina performed in 'The Sleeping Beauty Act III' with Pamela May as Florestan's Sisters and Kenneth MacMillan as Florestan. The front and back cover is designed by Oliver Messel depicting a front cover scene of the auditorium of the Royal Opera House framed by foliage, swags and crowns and the initials GR and RF. The back cover depicts the character Puss In Boots. The inside covers and main page of the programme are signed by members of the Sadler's Wells Ballet.
metadata.Related work: Symphonic Variations Façade The Sleeping Beauty

Related to letter ROH/VPP/1/01.

description: The certificate reads in Latin: 'Universis et Singulis in quâcunque dignitate constitutis quorum haec nosse interest, Senatus Inclitae Universitatis Aberdonensis S.J.D.S Noveritis nos eâ auctoritatequam summi ac potentissimi Principes Mmae huic Universitati amplissimam indulsere Tabellarum praesentium Latorem, Eruditione Insignem, Ninettam de Valois Ex Senatus Academici decreto, promovente Juris Facultatis Decano, omnibus, quae dignitatis ratio aut Academiae consuetudo postulat, rite peractis Utriusque Juris tam Canonici quam Civilis Doctorem et Magistrum Constituisse, creâsse, proclamâsse, renunciâsse; Nec non eidem potestatem fecisse docendi, legendi, scribendi, commentandi, omniaque id genus alia praestandi, quae hic aut alibi uspiam Juris Canonici et Civilis Doctoribus et Magistris concedi solent; Omnibusque honoribus, dignitatibus, et privilegiis ipsum affecisse et ornâsse, quibus affici et ornari solent qui ad illum dignitatis gradum ullibi terrarum legitimâ ratione evehuntur. Quod ut felix faustumque sit, Deum ter Opt. Max. comprecamur. In cuius rei fidem Tabellas hasce communi Universitatis Sigillo et Chirographis idoneis muniendas curavimus Aberdoniae Anno Salutis MCMLVIII die Mensis, quarto Julii'.
dimensions: (visible in mount) height 37 cm; (visible in mount) width 45 cm

title: Tutu worn by Galina Samsova as Odette in the Sadler's Wells Royal Ballet production of 'Swan Lake' (1981)
Tutu worn by Jane Landon as Odile in The Royal Ballet Touring Company production of 'Swan Lake' (1965)
description: Tutu with a black velvet boned bodice decorated with an appliquéd motif of gold thread and gold flower-shaped sequins on black net. The motif starts at the left back, runs along the front neckline and continues diagonally down to the left hip and onto the skirt. At the top right of the neckline is a sprig of wire covered in gold and ending in small opalescent pendent faux jewels. The skirt is layers of black net with scalloped edges, overlaid with the same decoration as the bodice. There are elastic shoulder straps, a strip of elastic in the gusset, and a metal hoop in the skirt.
creator: Leslie Hurry
condition: Good.The skirt has been crushed by storage. Visible rusting and corrosion to the metal tips of the boning and fastenings.

title: Tutu worn by Margot Fonteyn as The Firebird in the Sadler's Wells Ballet production of 'The Firebird' (1954)
description: Tutu with a boned bodice of red rayon grosgrain decorated with feather-shaped lines of gold cord and hand-painted with a darker red. The central V panel of the bodice is decorated with appliquéd gold and white crin hand-painted with purple. At two points on the neckline are plumes of thin red ostrich feathers. The centre back of the bodice is appliquéd with a panel of dark blue crin. The bottom edge of the bodice has scallop edges which overlay the skirt. The skirt has under layers of tarlatan graduating from pale pink to bright pink. The top layer of the skirt is made of flame-shaped tongues of yellow, orange and red rayon grosgrain each edged in gold thread, and tongues of gold and white crin. The skirt is also decorated with red feathers, and pieces of frayed red and yellow silk. At the back of the skirt are two wing shapes made of boned panels of gold, white and dark blue crin that are hand-painted red, pink and blue. The bodice has pink elastic shoulder straps and fastens with hooks and eyes. The skirt has crotch elastic. Worn with headdress ROH/PRO/COS/0000037 and earrings ROH/PRO/COS/0002345.
creator: Natalia Goncharova
condition: Good.The elastic of the shoulder straps has started to perish.

description: Tutu with a boned bodice of white satin. The top edge of the bodice is trimmed with silver lace and the bust area is overlaid with white organza and decorated with vertical stripes of diamanté on black cord. The bodice is heavily decorated with appliquéd black and silver braid, black and silver cord, faux pearls and diamanté in diamond and zigzag patterns. The lower edge of the bodice extends over the skirt and is trimmed with a frill of pleated white and silver striped organza. The skirt is layers of white net with scalloped edges, and a shorter overskirt of silver net decorated with two zigzag lines of black lace and white and silver crin ribbon. The lower line is decorated with rectangular rhinestones.

title: Tutu worn by the character The Fairy of Honour in the Prologue of The Royal Ballet production of 'The Sleeping Beauty' (1968)
description: Tutu with a chemise and short puffed sleeves of silver lurex and a boned corset of silver stretch lamé. The scooped neckline of the chemise is outlined in individually sewn silver balls and silver sequins. The corset has a trim of gold braid at the top and is decorated with diamanté, faux amber beads, silver circular and fleur-de-lys shaped sequins down the bodice and at the centre front and back. The botton edge of the bodice has a trim of silver foil edged in gold braid, and silver sequins. At the centre front is a large diamanté encircled with faux amber stones and outlined in gold braid. The underskirt is layers of pink scalloped nylon net overlaid with silver lurex decorated with silver sequins. There are two gold lurex embroidered lions rampant appliquéd to the centre front of the skirt, overlaid by a silver and black lurex short sword decorated with silver sequins. The skirt also has appliquéd decorations of silver lurex fleur-de-lys shapes sewn with silver sequins.
creator: Lila de Nobili

title: Tutu worn by Anya Linden as Sylvia in Act III of The Royal Ballet production of 'Sylvia' (1952)
description: Tutu with a boned bodice of salmon-pink polyester. Along the top of the bodice is a draped band which runs across the top of the arms and around to the back. The band is trimmed with a gold braid fringe and is decorated with a Greek key pattern in gold braid outlined in black paint. There are pink elastic shoulder straps and the right strap has a wire attached to it decorated with white plastic flowers. There is a right-hand short sleeve of salmon-pink polyester edged in gold ribbon. At the centre front of the bodice is a lozenge-shaped decoration with a vertical line of sequins and clear beads surrounded by hand-painted lines. Either side of the decoration is a vertical line of hand-painted Greek key patterns in gold and black. The overskirt of salmon-pink polyester has an opening at the front and is decorated down the two front edges and along the bottom edge with a Greek key pattern. It also has a palm leaf motif in gold braid highlighted with white and black hand-painting and silver sequins. The bottom edge of the overskirt is trimmed with a gold braid fringe partially painted silver. The skirt is layers of white net with scalloped edges. There is an elastic strap in the gusset.
creator: Robin Ironside
condition: Good.White paint has flaked off in many places. The bone in the centre front as come away from the bodice at the top.

The dress has a V neck edged in lace with a brown velvet bow at the centre, and a single row of velvet covered buttons down the centre front. The short wide sleeves are edged in bronze braid, as is the bodice. There are inner long sleeves of blue rayon. The full-length skirt of pale brown watermarked taffeta has a scalloped edge trimmed in bronze braid. title: Frock coat worn by Ann Murray as Octavian in Act II of The Royal Opera revival of 'Der Rosenkavalier' (1984)
description: White grosgrain frock coat heavily decorated with silver braid, iridescent white beads, and drops of beads to resemble small bunches of grapes. The sleeve cuffs are highly decorated with similar silver braiding and beads, and edged in silver ribbon. The back of the coat has a vent and two large pleats. The large pockets are edged in silver braid. The coat has a small stand-up collar. Worn with shirt ROH/PRO/COS/0003267.
creator: Maria Bjørnson
condition: Good.Glue used to secure some decoration has become discoloured. Some decoration has been removed.

On the left she is depicted wearing a silver domed helmet with two white feathered wings, a gold armlet, a full-length white sleeveless tunic, a white armoured corset, a white belt with gold decoration, a long white cloak, and thonged sandals. title: Cloak worn by Gré Brouwenstijn as Elizabeth de Valois in Act III scene 2 of the Covent Garden Opera Company production of 'Don Carlos' (1958)
description: Cloak of gold lamé with a V neck and a train. The cloak fastens down the front and is lined in blue jersey. It has medieval-style deep slashed sleeves over fitted inner sleeves. The outer sleeves are lined in old gold taffeta with printed hand-painted decoration. There are lines of gold lace trim down the front with gold filigree mock fasteners, which also hold the slashed sleeves. The three-inch gold lace trim starts in a V in the centre of the back, runs over the shoulders, down the front, around the edges above hem level, and out to the back of the train. The trim is set with large faux rubies. There is a white cotton frill at the neck and around the inner sleeves at the wrists. Worn with dress ROH/PRO/COS/0004210, underskirt ROH/PRO/COS/0004211, underskirt ROH/PRO/COS/0004212, and crown ROH/PRO/COS/0000190.

The upper layer is decorated with asymmetric blue horizontal stripes and gold beads, and the lower layer is decorated with horizontal mauve and black stripes. The sleeves are made from plain cerise silk with mauve cuff bands, and the dress has a cummerbund heavily decorated with jewels and edged with gold braid. title: Jacket worn by N Gillespie and Robert Byford as Prince Gremin in Act III scene 1 of The Royal Opera production of 'Eugene Onegin' (1971)
description: Black wool military-style jacket with a short front and stylised tails. The stand-up collar is of red wool edged in white wool crêpe and appliquéd with silver gilt stylised oak leaves. The gold epaulettes have gold fringing. The centre front panel of the jacket is of red wool outlined in gilt ribbon with large silver coloured buttons. The sleeves have deep red cuffs edged in white, with gilt appliquéd stylised leaf shapes and three buttons. The sash of silver gilt ribbon has a sword support and two tassels to the left. The jacket is lined in red chintz. The jacket tails have pocket flaps and three silver buttons, with two buttons to the base of the back. There is a deep vent to the centre back, turned back, with red wool edged in white.
creator: Julia Trevelyan Oman

title: Jacket worn by J Parry as a Captain in Act II scene 1 of The Royal Opera production of 'Eugene Onegin' (1971)
description: Military-style jacket in dark grey wool check with a green and red fleck. The jacket has a short front edged in silver gilt braid, and a stand-up collar decorated in silver gilt ribbon. The jacket has gold epaulettes, silver coloured buttons, and a star decoration on the left breast. The full-length sleeves with split pointed cuffs are decorated and edged in silver gilt ribbon. There are three false silver gilt braid buttonholes with three silver buttons. The jacket tails are turned back to reveal a white wool lining. They are edged in silver gilt ribbon and held with one silver coloured button. The pocket flaps have three buttons, and there are two buttons to the centre back. The label reads: Regina.

metadata.Scope and content: Negatives featuring Margaret Rawlings as Titania, Robert Helpmann as Oberon, Richard Ellis as Hymen, Margot Fonteyn and Michael Somes as Spirits of the Air, Moira Shearer as Attendant to Spring, Beryl Grey as Summer, Audrey Bowman as Attendant to Night, and Michael Hordern as Bottom, with members of the Sadler's Wells Ballet and Covent Garden Opera Company. Wood's negative register labels rolls 87F/1, 87F/2 and 87F/3 'dress rehearsal' and rolls 87F/4, 87F/5 and 87F/6 'matinée'. title: Signed and dated costume design by Attilio Comelli - Marguerite in Acts I, II and III of 'Faust'
description: Three watercolour and pencil designs for Marguerite. The half length design for Act I depicts her wearing a pink and white headdress, a short cape that has wide bands of dark blue and pale blue, a white shift and a white bodice with laced stays. The full-length design for Act II depicts her wearing a headdress of two pink, rounded horns, with a short white veil at the back, a white shift worn beneath a long pale blue gown with a laced bodice, full sleeves tied at the elbow and wrist with a blue and gold decorative border around the hem and bodice edge, and a narrow cream-coloured apron. There is a thumbnail design of the decorative border. The full-length design for Act III depicts her wearing a brown and grey headdress, a full-length grey gown with a laced bodice worn with a high-necked white shift, a full-length light brown cloak lined in grey, with a darker brown band near the hem and around the shoulders. The wearer name noted on the front of the design is: Madm Edwina. A handwritten note on the front of the design reads: '1 costume in grey. 1 small cape. 1 big cloak' and 'Piping same hue as gown'.
creator: Attilio Comelli

title: Signed and dated costume design by Attilio Comelli - Faust in 'Faust'
description: Watercolour and pencil design for Faust who is depicted wearing a dark purple velvet bonnet, a purple velvet and silk mid-length tunic with a pleated skirt, large, full sleeves of purple and gold brocade which narrow toward the cuff, and are laced to the tunic, a white undershirt and a gold and yellow brocade waistcoat worn beneath the tunic, dark purple velvet hose and slippers, and pale purple garters at the knees. He has a beard and blonde hair in a pageboy hairstyle. A handwritten note on the front of the design reads: 'Velvet tunic - silk trimming. [sham] brocade purple and gold. Waistcoat and undersleeves if possible yellow and gold brocade. Silk scarf to hold sword'. The rest of the note is unclear.

With annotations and pencil thumbnail sketches of decorative patterns.

title: Poster for the Royal Italian Opera performance of a 'Grand Concert' on 30 May 1849 at the Royal Italian Opera, Covent Garden
description: Poster with black and green text, listing the participants as below. The poster announces that the singers will perform extracts from the operas 'Semiramide', 'Lucrezia Borgia', 'Il barbiere di Siviglia', 'Don Giovanni', 'Lucia di Lammermoor', 'Don Pasquale', 'Masaniello' ('La Muette de Portici'), and 'Les Huguenots'. The 'Celebrated Pianist' Alexander Dreyschock will play a fantasia, 'the extraordinary Performer on the Contrabasso' Giovanni Bottesini will perform a solo, and The Hungarian Vocalists will sing 'two of their favorite morceaux between the acts'. The orchestra perform the overtures to 'Leonora', 'Semiramide', and 'A Midsummer Night's Dream'. The full chorus sings the 'Celebrated Prayer (without Accompaniment) from the Market Scene in 'Masaniello'.' The concert commences at half-past one.

The pointed sleeve heads are heavily decorated with gold cord and gold braid leaf shapes with pearls and sequins. The front of the tunic and the neck are outlined in gold and silver brocade, with leaf decoration as on the sleeves. The tunic has a corded belt outlined in silver braid, with a leaf shape decoration on the front.

title: Roger Wood Photographic Collection
creator: Roger Wood
condition: Good. A section of the 4" x 5" black and white negatives exhibit vinegar syndrome and have been scanned.

metadata.Date notes: Materials have been dated from Wood’s negative registers or from research. A number of prints are dated on the back.
metadata.Extent: Black and white prints: 334 files of large prints and contact sheets; 158 files of proof prints. Black and white negatives: 230 files of 2.25" x 2.25"; 77 files of 4" x 5"; 45 files of 35mm (to date). Colour transparencies: 20 files of 2.25" x 2.25"; 37 files of 4" x 5"; 14 files of 35mm. 115 glass negatives. 16 files of documents (to date)
metadata.Scope and content: The collection contains prints, negatives, and colour transparencies of ballet, opera, and drama productions and portraits of dancers, singers, actors, authors, painters, and TV personalities. The majority of the collection concerns the resident companies of the Royal Opera House, and its touring ballet company. Wood’s photographs cover the Sadler's Wells Ballet/The Royal Ballet from 1946 to 1967, the Covent Garden Opera Company from 1946 to 1965, and the Sadler's Wells Theatre Ballet/The Royal Ballet Touring Company from 1946 to 1957. Wood also photographed other opera companies, such as the D'Oyly Carte Opera Company, the Glyndebourne Opera Festival, and La Scala Opera, and other ballet companies, such as de Basil’s Ballet Russe, Ballet Rambert, Grand Ballet de Monte Carlo, Kirov Ballet, New York City Ballet, Paris Opera Ballet, and the Royal Danish Ballet. In addition, he took studio portraits of many dancers, both in The Royal Ballet and in other companies. His photographs of drama companies are predominantly of the Old Vic and Royal Shakespeare Company. The collection also contains all Wood's photographs of Peter Hall's 1983 production of the Ring Cycle in Bayreuth, which led to the book 'The Ring: Anatomy of an Opera'. In the collection are Wood’s negative registers, some exhibition catalogues, papers relating to the negatives Wood deposited at the New York Dance Archives, and papers relating to 'The Ring' book.
metadata.Creator: Roger Wood
metadata.History/biography: British photographer Roger Wood (1920-2005) specialised in theatre photography and was particularly well known for his photographs of ballet. Born Alexander Roger Wood in Madras, India, on 6 August 1920, he attended Bradfield College, Berkshire, and became interested in photography at a young age. After World War II, his first photographic job was for Kodak as film production controller. In 1948, Wood left Kodak to set up his own photographic studio in Kensington. During this time, he photographed many leading ballet, opera and drama companies, and contributed to a number of books on these subjects. He frequently photographed productions at the Royal Opera House, as well as dancers in the Sadler's Wells Ballet, particularly Margot Fonteyn. From the 1960s and 1970s, he produced several books on North Africa and the Middle East. From 1974 to 1988, he also worked as photographic consultant to the Ministry of Information in Oman, and his advice and photographs helped to establish the national museums in Muscat, Doha, and Riyadh. He was an active photojournalist, working for Picture Post and Sie und Er, and contributing to the Sunday Times. After gaining a pilot’s licence, he worked for Sir Alexander Gibb and Partners, and other engineering firms taking aerial photographs. He was a Fellow of the Institute of British Photographers, the Royal Society of Arts and the Photographic Society. He married his wife Rosemary in 1986. Wood died on 21 June 2005.
metadata.Archival history: Wood gave each exposure of the black and white negatives a unique reference number, which he usually noted on the back of the corresponding print to allow cross-referencing between prints and negatives. The 2.25” x 2.25” negatives have a code of four or five digits prefixed with an A, and the 4" x 5" negatives a code of four or five digits prefixed with a C (for example, A32164, C6532). These numbers have been transferred to the catalogue as 'photographer's own reference number' on both the prints and the negatives catalogue records. Wood’s negative registers list the reference codes in numerical order regardless of the initial letter. The 35mm reference numbers have a six character code relating to the roll of film and the exposure. For example, 87V/320 reads as roll of film 87V/3, frame 20. For the purposes of cataloguing the negatives, the reference code is recorded only as the roll, e.g., 87V/3, while the records for the prints give the full code for each print, e.g., 87V/320. The 35mm negatives were housed in albums with paper inserts that act as the negative register. The initial numbers of Wood’s code explain the genre. For example, 82 was opera (albums 82, 182, 282) and 87 was ballet (87, 187, 387, 487). Wood did not give the colour transparencies and glass negatives reference codes, and the collection does not contain registers for these materials.
metadata.Source of acquisition: Roger Wood bequeathed his archive to ROH Collections, along with the copyright. His widow, Rosemary Wood, deposited the archive in 2006.
metadata.System of arrangement: The collection is arranged into five categories: black and white prints, black and white negatives, colour transparencies, glass negatives, and documents. Roger Wood divided his print collection into files of large prints of varying sizes, with contact sheets, and files of small proof prints (4.5" x 6.5"). The black and white negatives and colour transparencies are also divided according to size: 2.25" x 2.25", 4" x 5", and 35mm. Wood stored his archive in a variety of files and drawers, which in general were organised by physical format, then by company and production. This original structure was retained but refined into a specific genre order: opera, ballet, drama, other. Within opera, the Royal Opera House's resident company is always first, followed by other companies in alphabetical order. Within ballet, the Royal Opera House's resident company is first, followed by its touring company, other companies in alphabetical order, and ballet artists. Drama companies and other areas are ordered alphabetically by company, followed by people. Within each company, files are arranged alphabetically by work and then chronologically by production.
metadata.Access conditions: The collection is available for viewing in ROH Collections by appointment only. Original prints and paper materials are accessible. The negatives may be viewed at the discretion of staff.
metadata.Copyright: Copyright is owned by Royal Opera House Collections.

dimensions: visible image: (excluding photographer's label) height 218 mm; visible image: width 170 mm; label: height 34 mm; label: width 145 mm

metadata.Date notes: Print dated from inscription.
metadata.Scope and content: Full-length portrait of Sanderson in a long floral patterned dress with a train, and feather headdress, holding a fan. In black ink on the base of the image, Sanderson has written: 'Sibyl Sanderson. To Lady de Grey, souvenir of 'Manon' in London May 30th 1891'. Lady de Grey's label reads: 'Sibyl Sanderson a perfect Manon.' The photographic studio is Dupont, 109 Rue Neuve, Brussels. The photograph was originally in album volume 1, page 33.

title: Unsigned and undated costume design by Attilio Comelli - Citizen Woman in 'La bohème'
description: Watercolour and pencil costume design for an elderly Citizen Woman who is depicted wearing a black poke bonnet with pink lining and ribbon, a frilled white cap worn beneath the bonnet, a bright green gown with a deep frill at the hem, leg-of-mutton sleeves, a frilled black bodice with a black bow at the waist and a high white collar. She wears a pink shawl, and white gloves. To the side of the design are two thumbnails detailing the side profile of a bonnet and some bows. Includes three fabric swatches of a green and pink wool check, a green, black, and white crepe check, and a terracotta wool attached to the front of the design.
creator: Attilio Comelli
condition: Good.The fabric swatches are still attached to the design board with the original large staples.

title: Unsigned and undated costume design by Attilio Comelli - Grisettes in 'La bohème'
description: Watercolour and pencil design for two Grisettes. The character on the left is depicted wearing pink hair ribbons, a pink gingham dress with a frilled hem, leg-of-mutton sleeves with white cuffs, and a wide collar, worn over a white blouse. The gown has a pink sash and is worn with a black apron. She wears a black shawl. The character on the right is depicted wearing a black frilly cap, a floral print gown of pale green, white, and pink, with a high collar, leg-of-mutton sleeves, and a frilled hem, and a cream pinafore apron. She wears a pink shawl. Includes two thumbnails detailing alternative bodices. One in mid-blue with a wide white collar, and the other a pale blue sailor-boy style bodice with dark blue trimming and bows. Includes two fabric swatches of a pink and white cotton gingham, and a white, pink and green floral print cotton attached to the front of the design. A handwritten note on the front of the design is unclear.
creator: Attilio Comelli
condition: Good.The fabric swatches are still attached to the design board with the original large staples.

title: Liyakat Misani (Honour of Merit) brooch miniature presented to Ninette de Valois by the President of the Republic of Turkey
description: Brooch in the shape of a gold-plated rectangular bar with white enamel, bearing the initials 'TC' (Türkiye Cumhuriyeti - Turkish Republic). At its centre is an enamelled miniature of the Liyakat Misani medal: a blue, gold-plate, white and yellow star containing an artist's palette, a quill pen, and a microscope over which is a small red circle containing the Islamic motif of a star and crescent moon. Related to medal ROH/VAL/BEQ/68, presentation case ROH/VAL/BEQ/69, and certificate ROH/VAL/BEQ/53.

title: Liyakat Misani (Honour of Merit) medal conferred upon Ninette de Valois by the President of the Republic of Turkey
description: Five-pointed silver star decorated with white and blue enamel and gold plating. Imposed on the star, at the top, is a red and white enamel boss with the Islamic motif of the star and crescent moon, edged in a wreath holding the letters 'TC' (Türkiye Cumhuriyeti - Turkish Republic). Imposed on the centre of the star, within a wreath of green enamel, are symbols of art, science and literature: an artist's palette, a quill and a microscope. The medal hangs without ribbon from a decorated brooch bar in white enamel edged in gold. The un-enamelled reverse carries in relief the letters 'TC Liyakat Misani'. Given in presentation case ROH/VAL/BEQ/69, and related to brooch miniature ROH/VAL/BEQ/72, and certificate ROH/VAL/BEQ/53.

title: Companion of the Order of the Companions of Honour Badge conferred upon Ninette de Valois by Her Majesty Queen Elizabeth II
description: Gilded bronze oval medal surmounted by a crown. The central gold plaque, depicting a mounted knight in armour, is enclosed in a blue enamel band bearing in gold the motto of the Order, 'In Action Faithful and in Honour Clear'. The reverse of the Badge is plain except for the crowned cipher of the monarch ('EIIR') in relief. The Badge is suspended via a plain ring from a red ribbon edged with gold thread fashioned into a bow, as it is a lady's award. The ribbon has a brooch attachment on the reverse. The Badge is worn at the left shoulder. Given in presentation case ROH/VAL/BEQ/48, and related to certificate ROH/VAL/BEQ/46 and file of papers ROH/VAL/BEQ/49.

title: Erasmus Prize certificate presented to Ninette de Valois by the Praemium Erasmianum Foundation, and related papers and presentation folder
description: Erasmus Prize certificate housed in a dark red leatherette folder with the lettering 'EP' embossed in gold on the front cover. The certificate reads (in Latin): 'Amstelodami, die xxi mensis iunii anni mcmlxxiv DECRETUM Altissimus Princeps Regius Neerlandiae ex articulo ii legis Fundationis cui nomen PRAEMIUM ERASMIANUM, quo statuitur in singulos annos praemium praemiave decerni iis sive hominibus sive institutionibus qui humano cultui, societati, scientiis inserviant, itaque Europae unitatem vel unificationem strenue adauxerint aut in operibus suis demonstraverint, convenienter iis quae de mercedis usu in dispositionibus de praemiis adiudicandis praescribuntar, auditis etiam Viris consiliariis, confirmavit Moderatorum sententiam qua placuit ut PRAEMIUM ERASMIANUM ANNI MCMLXXIV decerneretur feminae clarissimae NINETTE DE VALOIS idque de causis quae separatim expositae sunt. QUIBUS DE CAUSIS PRAEMIUM ERASMIANUM ADIUDICETUR Feminae clarissimae NINETTE DE VALOIS praemium decernitur quia uno et perpetuo animi sui tenore id quod sibi aetate iam prisca proposuerat consecuta est, ut in Britannia societatem morem classicum secutorum conderet quae multis exemplo esset; quia rectam et veram viam secuta scholis saltatoriis quae per omnes nationes cognoscerentur conditis fundamenta, quibus haec res bene eveniret, iacuit; quia opera indefessa fiduciaque quam facultatum sociorum operis semper habebat effecit ut ei existerent et duces et magistri saltatorum qui toto orbe terrarum copiam sui facerent; quia non solum in omni genere plurimum ob omnibus postularet sed etiam ardore humanitatis suae exemploque excelso saltationis, choreographiae, institutionis et discipulos et saltatores et choreographos instigavit ut artem corde diligerent eiusque summum fastigium adipiscerentur'. The related papers are: a programme for the Erasmus prize-giving ceremony in Amsterdam on 21 June 1974; three typed copies, one annotated, of the address given by de Valois at the prize-giving ceremony; letters between Ninette de Valois and G Sluizer of the Praemium Erasmianum Foundation regarding travel arrangements to the ceremony and the distribution of the prize money, 17 December 1973 - 26 November 1974. Related to commemorative books ROH/VAL/BEQ/32.

The certificate reads (in Latin): 'Amstelodami, die xxi mensis iunii anni mcmlxxiv DECRETUM Altissimus Princeps Regius Neerlandiae ex articulo ii legis Fundationis cui nomen PRAEMIUM ERASMIANUM, quo statuitur in singulos annos praemium praemiave decerni iis sive hominibus sive institutionibus qui humano cultui, societati, scientiis inserviant, itaque Europae unitatem vel unificationem strenue adauxerint aut in operibus suis demonstraverint, convenienter iis quae de mercedis usu in dispositionibus de praemiis adiudicandis praescribuntar, auditis etiam Viris consiliariis, confirmavit Moderatorum sententiam qua placuit ut PRAEMIUM ERASMIANUM ANNI MCMLXXIV decerneretur feminae clarissimae NINETTE DE VALOIS idque de causis quae separatim expositae sunt. QUIBUS DE CAUSIS PRAEMIUM ERASMIANUM ADIUDICETUR Feminae clarissimae NINETTE DE VALOIS praemium decernitur quia uno et perpetuo animi sui tenore id quod sibi aetate iam prisca proposuerat consecuta est, ut in Britannia societatem morem classicum secutorum conderet quae multis exemplo esset; quia rectam et veram viam secuta scholis saltatoriis quae per omnes nationes cognoscerentur conditis fundamenta, quibus haec res bene eveniret, iacuit; quia opera indefessa fiduciaque quam facultatum sociorum operis semper habebat effecit ut ei existerent et duces et magistri saltatorum qui toto orbe terrarum copiam sui facerent; quia non solum in omni genere plurimum ob omnibus postularet sed etiam ardore humanitatis suae exemploque excelso saltationis, choreographiae, institutionis et discipulos et saltatores et choreographos instigavit ut artem corde diligerent eiusque summum fastigium adipiscerentur'. The related papers are: a programme for the Erasmus prize-giving ceremony in Amsterdam on 21 June 1974; three typed copies, one annotated, of the address given by de Valois at the prize-giving ceremony; letters between Ninette de Valois and G Sluizer of the Praemium Erasmianum Foundation regarding travel arrangements to the ceremony and the distribution of the prize money, 17 December 1973 - 26 November 1974. Related to commemorative books ROH/VAL/BEQ/32.

metadata.History/biography: Spanish mezzo-soprano Conchita Supervia (1895-1936) made her debut in 1910 in Buenos Aires with the Spanish Opera Company. Whilst in Argentina she performed in 'Blanca de Beaulieu' and 'Los amantes de Teruel' and featured as Lola in 'Cavalleria rusticana'. The following year she performed the most prominent role of her early career: Octavian in 'Der Rosenkavalier' at the Costanzi Theatre in Rome. In 1912 she sang the role of Carmen at the Gran Teatre del Liceu in her hometown of Barcelona. It was a role she was identified with for the rest of her career. Supervia starred again as Carmen in Havana in 1914, where she also appeared in 'Mignon' and 'La Favorita'. In the 1915/16 winter season, she sang Carmen again with the Chicago Opera Association, also appearing in the title role in 'Mignon' and as Charlotte in 'Werther'. For the next fifteen years Supervia confined her performances to Spain and Italy. This period saw her establish a strong association with Rossini mezzo-soprano roles, including Angelina in 'La Cenerentola', Isabella in 'L'Italiana in Algeri' and Rosina in 'Il barbiere di Siviglia'. In January 1932 she undertook a two-month tour to North America, consisting of concert recitals in Washington, D.C., New York, Montreal and Kansas City and elsewhere, and performances of 'Carmen' in Chicago and Boston. In 1931 she moved to London and married timber broker Benzion Rubinstein. In 1934 she made her Royal Opera House debut in 'La Cenerentola', and the following year appeared in 'Carmen', 'La Cenerentola' and 'L'Italiana in Algeri'. She had been engaged to appear in the Imperial League of Opera's 1935 autumn season at Covent Garden, but had to cancel her appearances as a result of her pregnancy. In addition to her opera career, Supervia made a number of recordings and appeared regularly in concert. She also starred in the Victor Saville film 'Evensong' in 1934. Supervia died during childbirth on 30 March 1936 at the age of 40. Sources: Sadie, S (ed.) Grove Dictionary of Opera, New York: MacMillan, 1992; record liner notes by Professor Stanley Henig at http://www. marstonrecords.com/supervia/supervia_liner.htm.; Rosenthal, Harold Two Centuries of Opera at Covent Garden, London, Putnam & Co, 1958.

The sleeves are in two parts. The top part of the sleeves are black velvet with a wide mustard yellow velvet stripe, and are trimmed along the top and bottom edge with mustard yellow velvet. They are attached to the jacket and to the bottom part of the sleeves with mustard yellow velvet laces. The lower part of the sleeves are black velvet trimmed along the top and bottom edge with mustard yellow velvet. There are eyelets and black laces at the cuff. Worn with breeches ROH/PRO/COS/0005947 and shirt ROH/PRO/COS/0005946. The wearer labels state that Roberto Alagna (in 1992) and [Stefano] Secco (in 2001) wore the jacket as the character Il. title: Tutu worn by Margot Fonteyn as The Firebird in the Sadler's Wells Ballet production of 'The Firebird' (1954)
description: Tutu with a boned bodice of red rayon grosgrain decorated with feather-shaped lines of gold cord and hand-painted with a darker red. The central V panel of the bodice is decorated with appliquéd flat black crin and a panel of flat white crin threaded with gold thread and topped with gold braid along the centre. At two points on the neckline are plumes of thin red ostrich feathers. The bodice has two panels of black net at the back. The skirt has under layers of scallop-edged nylon netting graduating from yellow to orange, with a top layer of pink. The top layer of the skirt is made of flame-shaped tongues of red, orange, and yellow rayon grosgrain edged with gold braid and backed in net; tongues of flat translucent crin threaded with gold thread, similar to the bodice decoration; thin red feathers; and orange and yellow ribbons. Some tongues also have gold braid down the middle. At the back of the skirt are two wire wings covered with tongues of gold crin and white crin threaded with gold thread; both have gold braid down the centre. The tongues nearest the waist have been painted red. The bodice has pink elastic shoulder staps and fastens with hooks and eyes. There is an elastic strap in the gusset. Worn with headdress ROH/PRO/COS/0000037 and earrings ROH/PRO/COS/0002345.
creator: Natalia Goncharova
condition: Good.The red satin has faded, particularly the tongues. The skirt is rather crushed.

description: Tutu with a boned bodice of dark salmon-pink silk tafetta. Along the top of the bodice is a draped band which runs across the top of the arms and around the back. The band is decorated with pink net embroidered with a Greek key pattern in black and gold thread. In the centre of the band and at two points over the arms are flower-shapes of blue jewels. At the centre front of the bodice is a lozenge-shaped decoration of pink net outlined in gold braid and with three teardrop blue gems. Either side of the decoration is a vertical line of embroidered Greek key patterns in black and gold thread on pink net. The overksirt of dark salmon-pink silk tafetta has an opening at the front and is decorated down the two front edges and along the bottom edge with a Greek key pattern and a palm leaf motif in embroidered gold and black thread on pink net with silver sequins. The palm leaf motifs are decorated with round and teardrop blue gems. The bottom edge of the overskirt is trimmed with a gold braid fringe. The skirt is layers of white net with pointed edges. There are pink elastic shoulder straps.

The skirt is layers of black net decorated on the top layer with gold and iridescent braid and iridescent sequins. Black feathers are sewn in between the top layers of the net. There are elastic shoulder straps, an elastic strap in the gusset, and a metal hoop in the skirt.
creator: Carl Toms

title: Dress worn by Edith Coates as The Countess in Act II of the Covent Garden Opera Company production of 'The Queen of Spades' (1950)
description: Salmon pink satin 18th-century court dress overlayed with chiffon net and highly decorated. The boned bodice has a stomacher and a low, scooped neckline. The side panels of the bodice are made of silver lurex with an overlay of fishnet, edged in gold and black brocade and decorated with rosettes of gold stars edged in red and black braid. The stomacher is decorated with rosettes of silver ribbon and braid. The half-length sleeves are finished with handkerchief points that have been stiffened. The underskirt is painted with an abstract design. The gathered overskirt is lined in pink fabric and decorated with a brown and gold rope with a tassel. Worn with underskirt ROH/PRO/COS/0003967 and headdress ROH/PRO/COS/0003799.
creator: Oliver Messel

title: Head and wings for the character Cockerel in The Royal Ballet production of 'La Fille mal gardée' (1960)
description: Buckram cockerel's head overlaid with cream and pale orange satin with hand-painted eye details and decorated with cream and yellow feathers. The comb and craw are red felt and the beak is yellow felt. Where the head attaches to the wings is a collar of pale orange satin with the edges cut into feather shapes and decorated with a feather pattern in black pen and with pink and black feathers. title: Tutu worn by Margot Fonteyn as The Sugar Plum Fairy in a BBC television production of 'Casse Noisette' ('The Nutcracker')
description: Tutu with a boned bodice of pink fabric shot with gilt thread. The top edge of the bodice is trimmed with gold crin. The front neckline and the centre front are decorated with silver braid, iridescent leaf-shaped sequins, pink pearlised beads, diamantés on wires, and teardrop rhinestones. The basque has one layer of pink and two layers of pale green silk with scalloped edging trimmed with silver cord and decorated with diamanté. The cap sleeves are two layers of scalloped pink and green fabric mounted on white tulle and white net. The sleeves are trimmed with silver cord and decorated with iridescent leaf-shaped sequins, diamanté, gold sequins, and pearlised beads. The skirt is layers of pink net with pointed edges, decorated with silver sequins. The top layer is pale pink net edged with gold and white crin ribbon, silver tinsel, silver sequins, diamanté, beads. It has appliquéd fan-shaped panels of pleated tulle hand-painted pink and decorated with silver and gold sequins and diamanté. There are elastic shoulder straps, an elastic strap in the gusset, and a hoop in the skirt. (Note: The ballet was broadcast on 21 December 1958. The producer was Margaret Dale. Peter Wright provided additional choreography. Michael Somes was The Prince.)
creator: Jane Scrase Dickens

The bottom edge of the bodice has scalloped edges overlaying the skirt. The skirt has under layers of nylon net graduating from purple to pale pink. The top layer of the skirt is made of flame-shaped tongues of red, yellow and orange rayon grosgrain, each edged in gold thread, and tongues of gold and white crin. The skirt is also decorated with pink and red feathers, pieces of frayed red and yellow silk, and gold sequins. At the back are wing shapes made of boned panels of gold and white crin hand-painted in pink. Both sides of the centre back bodice and skirt are decorated with a panel of black and gold crin. The bodice has pink elastic shoulder straps and fastens with hooks and eyes. There is an elastic strap in the gusset.
creator: Natalia Goncharova
condition: Good.The net of the skirt has been significantly trimmed. The skirt is slightly crushed. The gusset has been cut through.

title: Dress worn by Christine Keith and Marylyn Trounson as Attendant to The Lilac Fairy in The Royal Ballet production of 'The Sleeping Beauty' (1968)
description: Dress with a lavender silk bodice with a centre front panel of overlaid cream chiffon trimmed with gold lurex ribbon, cream artificial flowers and sequins. It has a false chemise of cream silk chiffon with short puffed sleeves and a gathered neckline, all trimmed with small faux pearl beads. A pair of wire and crystal organza wings are attached to the back of the bodice. The skirt has two underlayers of cream silk tulle of which the upper layer is decorated with appliquéd pearlised shapes and silver braid at the hem edge. The top layer of the skirt is lilac silk tulle decorated with silver sequins. The integral knickers are decorated with layers of crin and gathered net.

title: Headdress for the character of a Coryphée in Act II of The Royal Ballet production of 'Anastasia' (1971)
description: Two-tiered headdress. The lower tier is black mesh decorated with silver effect braid, strips of diamanté, and roundels of faux jet decorated with silver effect cord, A row of round faux clear gems hang from the bottom edge. Attached to the sides of the lower tier are faux earrings of roundels of silver lurex with a central jet gem surrounded by silver cord and diamanté. Hanging from the roundels are round clear gems and black jet pendant beads. Attached to both sides of the lower tier are three strands of diamanté set in black which attach to a small round wire frame which sits on the back of the hair. It is decorated with a small oval jewel of black jet surrounded by silver cord and diamanté, a single jet pendant bead, and a plume of black ostrich feathers. The lower tier is connected to the upper tier by five stiffened supports of silver braid decorated with bronze coloured sequins. The upper tier is a wire frame decorated with silver cord and strands of diamanté set in black. It has seven ovals of silver lurex and jet gems decorated with clear gems, silver cord, and diamanté. It fastens with black cotton ties.
creator: Barry Kay
dimensions: Crown: diameter 21 cm; Feathers: height 22 cm; Crown: height 19 cm

The upper tier is a wire frame decorated with silver cord and strands of diamanté set in black. It has seven ovals of silver lurex and jet gems decorated with clear gems, silver cord, and diamanté. It fastens with black cotton ties.

title: Tutu worn by Margot Fonteyn as Cinderella in Act II of the Sadler's Wells Ballet production of 'Cinderella' (1948)
description: Tutu with a boned bodice of white satinised cotton. The neckline is edged with a white net frill. The bust area is outlined with alternating diamanté and faux pearls and decorated with coloured faux jewels surrounded by diamanté or pearls. At the centre is a jewel of three large square diamanté surrounded by small round diamanté and with two faux pearl drop beads. The basque has scalloped edges decorated with pearls, and coloured faux jewels surrounded in diamanté or pearls. The underskirt is white tarlatan with unevenly cut edges and the top layer is decorated with silver sequins. The overskirt is white net decorated with silver sequins and sprays of cloth flowers in pink, yellow, blue, and white, and two pale blue crin rolls. There are elastic shoulder straps.
creator: Jean-Denis Malclès

title: Tutu worn by Margot Fonteyn as Princess Aurora in Act I of the Sadler's Wells Ballet production of 'The Sleeping Beauty' (1946)
description: Tutu with a bodice of salmon pink lurex. The bertha collar is gold-threaded crin decorated with silver embroidery and silver sequins. In the centre of the neckline is a rosette of red cotton organdie ribbon with baubles of white sequins hanging from silver cord. The bodice is decorated with appliquéd motifs of silver embroidery and silver sequins and has a band of silver crin running down the centre. The long sleeves are beige cotton net decorated with silver embroidery and silver sequins. At the tops of the sleeves is a rosette similar to that on the bodice, attached to the collar via elastic. The sleeves have crin cuffs. The skirt is made of layers of pink and orange cotton net with scalloped edges and overlaid with a layer each of salmon lurex and organza. The skirt is decorated with appliquéd silver lurex outlined in silver braid and with silver sequins. There are elastic shoulder straps and an elastic strap in the gusset.
creator: Oliver Messel

title: Tutu worn by Doreen Wells, Pamela Moncur, and Diana Vere as Princess Aurora's Friend in Act I of The Royal Ballet revival of 'The Sleeping Beauty' (1946)
description: Tutu with a pale blue sateen bodice with a collar of white crin and gold metallic ribbon worn off the shoulder. There is a rosette of pink ribbon in the centre front of the collar. It has a central decoration of gold crin and gold sequins, and two gold crin and gold sequin baubles. The centre front of the bodice is decorated with strips of white crin and gold braid in a V shape ending in a point at the waist with two gold baubles. The basque of pale blue sateen is decorated with bows of white crin with gold ribbon, and baubles of silver and gold sequins. The short sleeves of blue sateen are slashed to reveal beige elbow-length net with two rows of crin frills. The tops of the sleeves are decorated with gold bows and gold baubles. The underskirt is layers of lilac nylon net with scalloped edges.The top layer is pale blue chiffon laid over grey and black striped lining fabric, edged in white crin with a gold thread decoration. The skirt is decorated with foliage shapes of white crin and flower shapes of white muslin. There are small elastic shoulder straps, an elastic strap in the gusset, and a hoop in the skirt.
creator: Oliver Messel

Smaller blue velvet feather shapes extend up the elastic shoulder straps. Feathers are hand-painted on the bodice, basque, and skirt. The elastic shoulders straps are decorated with ruched white crin with gold thread, and the neckline is edged with a frill of the same. The skirt is layers of white net with scalloped edges. The overskirt is white nylon net over a layer of pale blue lurex, embroidered over the hips with white couching. The skirt is decorated with translucent sequins and leaf shapes. There is an elastic strap in the gusset.
creator: Oliver Messel

title: Tutu worn by Nadia Nerina as Princess Aurora in Act I of the Sadler's Wells Ballet production of 'The Sleeping Beauty' (1946)
description: Tutu with a boned bodice of salmon pink lurex. The bertha collar is gold-threaded crin decorated with silver embroidery and silver sequins. In the centre of the neckline is a rosette of red cotton organdie ribbon with baubles of white sequins hanging from silver cord. The bodice is decorated with appliquéd motifs of silver embroidery and silver sequins. It has a band of silver crin running down the centre front. The long sleeves are beige cotton net decorated with silver embroidery and silver sequins. At the tops of the sleeves is a rosette similar to that on the bodice, attached to the collar via elastic. The sleeves have crin cuffs. The skirt is made of layers of pink and orange cotton net with scalloped edges and overlaid with a layer each of salmon lurex and organza. The skirt is decorated with appliquéd motifs of silver lurex edged in silver braid and decorated with silver sequins. The hem edge of the skirt is trimmed with gold threaded crin. There are elastic shoulder straps, a strap in the gusset, and the skirt has a hoop.

title: Tutu for the character The Fairy of Beauty in the Prologue of The Royal Ballet production of 'The Sleeping Beauty' (1968)
description: Tutu with a boned bodice of gold lurex. The central panel is white faux fur decorated with silver sequins, gold flower-shaped sequins, diamanté, silver beads, gold hand-painting, and black diamond-shaped beads to simulate ermine. There is a large rhinestone in the centre of the neckline. The bodice is outlined in white faux fur with black diamond-shapped beads to simulate ermine, and this extends over the shoulder straps. Where the bodice and skirt meet at the sides are strips of silver and black embroidered ribbon, diamanté, and iridescent sequins. There are two poppers at the top of the back for attaching a cloak. The underskirt is layers of mauve net with scalloped edges. The top layer of skirt is gold lamé net decorated with gold sequins. The centre front of the skirt has an appliquéd panel of mauve net decorated with a band of silver ribbon, sequins, and gold braid edging. The skirt is also decorated with crown motifs made of silver braid and diamanté, and butterfly motifs of iridescent crystal organza, gold thread, and pearlised sequins. The bodice has eyelets at the back but the laces are missing.
creator: Lila de Nobili
condition: Good.The edge of the skirt is slightly crushed. The eyelets are rusting.

title: Tutu worn by Beryl Grey and Nadia Nerina as Sylvia in Act III of the Sadler's Wells Ballet production of 'Sylvia' (1952)
description: Tutu with a boned bodice of salmon-pink polyester. Along the top of the bodice is a draped band which runs across the top of the arms and around to the back. The band is trimmed with a gold braid fringe and is decorated with a Greek key pattern in gold braid outlined in black paint. On the centre front of the bodice is a lozenge-shaped decoration of a vertical line of sequins and clear beads surrounded by gold braid. Either side of the decoration is a vertical line of Greek key motifs in gold braid highlighted with black and white hand-painting. The overskirt of salmon-pink polyester has an opening at the front and is decorated down the two front edges and along the bottom edge with a Greek key pattern. It also has a palm leaf motif in gold braid highlighted with white and black hand-painting and silver sequins. The bottom edge of the overskirt is trimmed with a gold braid fringe partially painted silver. The skirt is layers of white net with scalloped edges. There is one elastic shoulder strap, a hoop in the skirt and an elastic strap in the gusset.
creator: Robin Ironside
condition: Fair.Paint has flaked off in several places.

title: Dress worn by Miss Edmunsen as a Noble Lady in a production of 'Roméo et Juliette'
description: Dress of gold damask devoré that has a floral pattern. There is a square neckline that is trimmed with a ruffle of cream silk and gold braid. The front and back panels of the bodice are laced together with gold cord. The under bodice has side panels visible beneath the lacings of a brighter gold damask. The sleeves are laced onto the bodice at the shoulders with gold cord. The sleeves are in two parts with the top part in bright gold damask edged in gold braid. The lower half of the sleeve is brown velvet edged with gold braid. The lower portions also have eyelets and lacings all down the outside edge. There are inset sleeves of a cream coloured chemise visible at the shoulders and between the upper and lower sleeves. There is an overskirt with front and back panels of darker gold damask and an underskirt of cream cloth that has side panels of brighter gold damask. The bodice fastens with hooks and eyes.
creator: Attilio Comelli

title: Signed and dated costume design by Attilio Comelli - The Devil and El Zanni in 'La Gioconda'
description: Watercolour and pencil design for the Devil and El Zanni. The Devil is depicted wearing a red hood with horns, a red blouson tunic with a red ruff, red harem pants, and red hose and slippers. El Zanni wears a tall green and yellow hat decorated with white feathers, a black mask with a beard, a white and green tunic, wide legged white trousers, green and white vertically striped hose, and white shoes with green bows. He is playing a mandolin. The note '3' for The Devil and '1' for El Zanni on the front of the design denotes the number of costumes to be made from this design.
creator: Attilio Comelli

title: Dress worn by Belinda Corken and Ann Howard as an Attendant to The Lilac Fairy in The Royal Ballet production of 'The Sleeping Beauty' (1968)
description: Dress comprising a lavendar silk bodice with a false shift and centre front panel of cream chiffon trimmed with gold coloured ribbon, cream artificial flowers and sequins. It has a false chemise of cream silk chiffon with short puffed sleeves and a gathered neckline, all trimmed with small faux pearl beads. A pair of wire and silver coloured organza wings are attached to the back of the bodice. The skirt has an outer layer of lilac silk tulle decorated with sequins, and two underlayers of cream silk tulle of which the upper layer is trimmed with silver coloured lace and appliquéd pearlised shapes. The integral knickers are trimmed with layers of crin and gathered net.
creator: Lila de Nobili

The bodice has an insert of orange and yellow pleated cotton tulle, and the skirt has an overlaid panel of the same fabric, both of which sit diagonally across the dress and meet at the waist. description: Pale grey corduroy tunic. The neckline is trimmed with white lace, dark gold braid, and round rhinestones. The centre front is decorated with appliquéd motifs of cream silk, and in the centre is an oval faux amethyst surrounded by round rhinestones. At the waist is a band of pleated yellow tafetta decorated with square rhinestones. The sleeve caps are pale grey corduroy edged with yellow tafetta binding. They are trimmed at the shoulder seam with dark gold braid and round rhinestones. The upper sleeves are ruffles of ivory organdie, and the lower sleeves are pale grey corduroy decorated with square and round rhinestones.

description: Purple grosgrain tafetta dress. It has a collar of gold lace and gold crin. At the centre front of the neckline is a gold jewel with green oval faux gems. The full-length sleeves have a deep frill of olive green taffeta at the elbow. The skirt has a bustle of olive green taffeta that extends in swags over the hips and in flounces down the front of the skirt. The flounces are decorated at the sides and front with orange and black ostrich feathers, loops of black crin ribbon, and rosettes of red, turquoise and olive striped braid with a faux gem in the centre. The centre front of the skirt is decorated with horizontal stripes of turquoise grosgrain ribbon and gold braid, and baubles of orange sequins. The hem edge is decorated with baubles of orange sequins.

Dress worn by Frederick Ashton as one of Cinderella's Stepsisters in Act II of the Sadler's Wells Ballet production of 'Cinderella' (1948)
description: Yellow grosgrain and tafetta dress. The square neckline is trimmed with a frill of white net and decorated with zigzags of black grosgrain ribbon. The yellow grosgrain bodice is decorated with a pattern of vertical lines of black ribbon, hand-painting, and appliquéd black rings. The bottom edge centre front of the bodice is decorated with a large pale blue satin bow. There is a peplum of yellow taffeta overlaid with yellow net. The bottom edge is decorated with black hand-painting, black sequins, and gold baubles. The sleeves are yellow taffeta overlaid with yellow net, decorated with vertical lines of black ribbon and a horizontal band of black velvet with oval sequins. The cuffs are trimmed with pale blue satin bows and a flounce of white net hand-painted with black spots. The yellow taffeta skirt is decorated with vertical strips of wide black velvet ribbon, and pale blue satin bows on each side. Three-quarters of the way down the skirt is a hoop, and the line of the hoop is decorated with a horizontal band of net hand-painted black and with pearlised oval sequins. There is a row of scalloped tabs of black velvet with hand-painted yellow lines. The lower section of the skirt is yellow taffeta with vertical strips of black velvet ribbon. The hem edge is trimmed with black tasseled braid and black wool pompoms.
creator: Jean-Denis Malclès

title: Dress for the character of the Queen in the Prologue and Act III the Sadler's Wells Ballet production of 'The Sleeping Beauty' (1946)
description: Grey and pink dress. The grey lurex bodice has a low and wide neckline decorated with piping and a frill of gold and white crin. The stomacher panel is decorated with gold and white crin, gold ribbon and diamanté. The dress has long sleeves slashed above the elbow to reveal grey lurex, and slashed below the elbows to reveal grey net and deep gathered cuffs. The openings are trimmed with gold effect ribbon and the cuffs are trimmed with gold effect ribbon and white cotton lace. The skirt is cut away to reveal an underskirt of pink taffeta with an overlayer of net cut into squares and decorated with gold ribbon and diamanté. The skirt layers are trimmed with white fringing. Worn with train ROH/PRO/COS/0002144.
creator: Oliver Messel

title: Dress worn by Angela Beveridge and Jacqueline Williams in the mazurka in Act III of the Sadler's Wells Ballet production of 'The Sleeping Beauty' (1946)
description: Full-length court dress with an off-the-shoulder neckline which is decorated with twisted white crin. The bodice, half-length puffed sleeves and overskirt are white and pink stripes decorated with strips of gold braid. The bodice is decorated with a swag of dark green satin and loops of gold ribbon. The undersleeves of white net are decorated with gold braid and the cuffs with white rope braid. The overskirt is decorated with bows of dark green satin at the side and back. The integral underskirt is yellow taffeta decorated with horizontal bands of gold braid. The Wardrobe Department labelled this costume 'Mazurka'.
creator: Oliver Messel

title: Dress worn by Kirsten Flagstad as Isolde in the Covent Garden Opera Company production of 'Tristan und Isolde' (1948)
description: Full-length medieval-style dress in rust-coloured silk velvet with a short semi-circular train. The neckline is trimmed with green satin ribbon decorated with appliquéd gold thread. The same ribbon runs in two lines down the front, framing the central panel. It has long oversleeves with a band of ribbon decoration around the top of the arm and at the cuff. There are long undersleeves in rust-coloured silk that end in a point over the hand. The dress is lined in rust-coloured silk. The belt of rust-coloured silk velvet is edged in gold metal thread ribbon and decorated with three glass aquamarines set in gold coloured decorative metal. The belt is made to appear to be tied with one end extending down the front of the costume. This costume was originally designed for a production from before World War II.
condition: Good.The silk lining is degrading particularly around the sleeves.

title: Tunic worn by Rudolf Nureyev as Prince Florimund in Act III of The Royal Ballet production of 'The Sleeping Beauty' (1968)
description: Brown silk velvet tunic. The neckline, centre front edge and armhole openings are decorated with a copper-coloured lurex trim. The back of the tunic is plain and the front is decorated with heraldic emblems in gold lurex, gold brocade and gold lace. The dagged epaulettes are trimmed with gold braid lace and pink and blue sequins. The bottom edge is dagged and decorated with gold braid lace and pink and blue sequins. The full-length sleeves are decorated at the cuffs with a copper-coloured lurex trim. The tunic is lined with chestnut brown lining fabric, and fastens at the centre front with hooks and eyes and had a gold lamé placket. The dagged hem and epaulettes are lined with brown moleskin. The sleeves are lined with coffee-coloured grosgrain.
creator: Lila de Nobili

title: Headdress for the character of a Coryphée in The Royal Ballet production of 'Anastasia' (1971)
description: Two-tiered headdress. The lower tier is black mesh decorated with silver effect braid, strips of diamanté, and roundels of faux jet decorated with silver effect cord, A row of round faux clear gems hang from the bottom edge. Attached to the sides of the lower tier are faux earrings of roundels of silver lurex with a central jet gem surrounded by silver cord and diamanté. Hanging from the roundels are round clear gems and black jet pendant beads. Attached to both sides of the lower tier are three strands of diamanté set in black which attach to a small round wire frame which sits on the back of the hair. It is decorated with a small oval jewel of black jet surrounded by silver cord and diamanté, a single jet pendant bead, and a plume of black ostrich feathers. The lower tier is connected to the upper tier by five stiffened supports of silver braid decorated with bronze coloured sequins. The upper tier is a wire frame decorated with silver cord and strands of diamanté set in black. It has seven ovals of silver lurex and jet gems decorated with clear gems, silver cord, and diamanté. It fastens with black cotton ties. Worn with choker ROH/PRO/COS/0000388.
creator: Barry Kay
condition: Fair.Parts of the diamanté are coming unstuck, and some larger beads are loose.

The poster states that this performance is for the benefit of the Fund for the Relief of the Distressed Irish and Scotch, and 'in the course of the evening will be sung a lyrical ode written and composed expressly for the occasion'. Paul Taglioni choreographed 'Coralia' to music by Cesare Pugni, with scenery by Charles Marshall, the appointments by Edmund Bradwell, and costumes by Miss Bradley and Mr Whales under the superintendance of Mademoiselle Copére.

title: Poster for a performance of the opera 'The Castle of Andalusia' and the comedy 'Charles the Second' on 27 May 1829 at the Theatre Royal, Covent Garden
description: Poster with black and red text, listing the cast as below. The poster states that this performance is a 'Benefit in Aid of the Funds of the Printers' Pension Society, for the Relief of Aged & Distressed Printers and their Widows' and that 'in the course of the Evening, an Address will be Spoken by Mr Keely in the Character of a Printer's Devil'. Between the opera and play is a 'musical melange' of songs and a piano concerto. The poster also announces the forthcoming performances of the comedy 'The Suspicious Husband' and masque 'Comus' on 28 May; the operas 'The Marriage of Figaro' ('Le nozze di Figaro'), 'Clari' and 'Giovanni in London' (Act I) on 29 May; the comedy 'The Beaux Strategem', divertissement 'Auld Robin Gray' and play 'The Invincibles' on 30 May; the play 'Romeo and Juliet' on 1 June; the opera 'Der Freischütz' on 2 June performed by Mr Schütz's German Company; and the opera 'The Maid of Judah' on 5 and 20 June.

title: Headdress for the character Scorpio in the Sadler's Wells Royal Ballet production of '6.6.78' (1978)
description: Buckram cap covered with black lurex velvet. At the centre front is a green plastic jewel surrounded by blue, green, and gold sequins and green metallic braid. The front claws are black crin tubes filled with red, green, blue, and gold sequins, and the pincers are white crin tubes painted pink and filled with pink and orange sequins. They have pink metallic ribbon wrapped around the ends. The six legs are white crin tubes painted gold and filled with red and gold sequins and gold braid. In two places, they are wrapped with wire, which pulls in the crin to create the joints of the leg. Pink metallic ribbon is wound round the ends. The tail is a black crin tube filled with red sequins. In five places, thin bands of black lurex velvet wrap around and pull in the crin to create joints. Pink metallic cord runs along the top and bottom edge of the tail and forms the sting at the end.
creator: Ian Spurling
